detailFootnote: Maximum drawdown uses complete closes from September 22 to October 30. Rebound profit retained = (October 30 price - July 29 price) / (September 22 price - July 29 price), defined only for positive rebounds. A negative value means all rebound profit was lost; above 100% means further gains. First threshold hits count trading days and do not imply that the gain was sustained.

introLead: A drawdown, a rebound, and another drawdown. Compare 78 AI-related US stocks and ETFs with NVIDIA over the same three windows.
introScope: Eight categories: AI applications, Agent Infra, consumer electronics, Neocloud, compute, optical interconnects, memory & storage, and grid & modular power.
introFoot: Dates are shared across securities, not chosen to favor each stock. July 29 was identified in hindsight as NVDA's lowest July closing price.

methodShort: All prices are updated through the October 30, 2026 regular-session close. 77 securities use Futu OpenD forward-adjusted daily prices; KXIAY uses Yahoo Finance adjusted daily prices. Returns are price changes, exclude taxes and trading costs, and are not exact dividend-reinvestment total returns. Annualized volatility is the sample standard deviation of daily returns from July 1 to October 30 multiplied by the square root of 252. Maximum drawdowns use complete closing prices.
methodLimits: This is one historical cycle with boundaries chosen in hindsight. The universe and categories are curated; category memberships and ETF holdings overlap. Medians are not investable portfolio returns, and correlations are neither causal claims nor probabilities of future outcomes.

research.title: Beyond rebound rankings: where did returns diverge?
research.intro: The analysis below uses 75 securities with complete three-phase histories. LYTE, NCLD, and SKHY remain in the data explorer but are excluded from full-cycle groups and rankings.

cards.label: Positive full-period returns
cards.note: The remaining securities were still below their June-end prices.

cards.note: The denominator includes only securities that rose during the rebound.

research.categoryTitle: 01 / The split is in retained value, not just rebound size
research.categoryBody: Agent Infra had a median full-period return of {agentTotal}, with {agentPositive}/{agentCount} securities gaining. Neocloud, optical interconnects, and memory & storage had medians of {neoTotal}, {opticalTotal}, and {memoryTotal}. Only {computePositive}/{computeCount} compute securities finished positive. An AI theme label cannot substitute for examining the path of losses and retained gains.
research.categoryNote: Each column is the median of the category's complete histories. Memberships overlap, so category counts cannot be added. Compounding the three phase medians does not produce the full-period median.
research.tradeoffTitle: 02 / The strongest rebound group then suffered a deeper decline
research.tradeoffBody: In the selected {sampleName} sample ({sampleN} securities), the top rebound quartile had a median rebound of {upperRally}, followed by {upperD2} in phase 3; the weakest quartile returned {lowerD2} in phase 3. Their median annualized volatilities were {upperVol} and {lowerVol}. The rebound/phase-3 rank correlation was {rhoAll}, and remained {rhoEquity} after excluding ETFs. This describes risk in one sample, not the next cycle.
research.scatterHint: The dashed lines intersect at NVDA. Upper-right points had both larger rebounds and higher subsequent returns. Select a point to examine path risk. ETFs and stocks may overlap and are not independent observations.
research.quartileNote: Groups run from the weakest to strongest rebound, with roughly equal counts. Values are medians, not portfolio returns.
research.robustTitle: 03 / Four three-phase leaders, with a conditional low-risk advantage
research.robustBody: MSFT, CRM, PLTR, and OKTA outperformed NVDA in all three baseline windows; only MSFT had lower historical volatility. Moving the boundary from July 29 to July 31 changes MSFT's rebound from {msftRally} to {msftMonth}, below NVDA's {nvdaMonth}. CRM, PLTR, and OKTA remain ahead in all three phases under both definitions, but their volatilities are about {crmRatio}, {pltrRatio}, and {oktaRatio} times NVDA's. No security met both conditions: leading in every phase under both date definitions and not increasing historical volatility.
research.robustNote: Ordered by historical volatility, with NVDA as the reference. The alternative split moves the phase-1/rebound boundary from July 29 to July 31; phase 3 is unchanged. This is a historical screen, not a forecast ranking.
research.retentionTitle: 04 / Similar rebounds can leave very different amounts of capital
research.retentionBody: TEM and SNDK both rebounded about 86%. Yet 100 invested in each on June 30 ended at {temEnd} and {sndkEnd}, respectively. TEM retained {temRetained} of its rebound profit, versus {sndkRetained} for SNDK and {nvdaRetained} for NVDA. TEM still had a {temDD} maximum closing drawdown in phase 3, versus {nvdaDD} for NVDA. Better recovery and greater path risk can coexist.
research.retentionNote: Initial-loss recovery measures July 29 to September 22; rebound-profit retention measures what remained after September 22. The denominators differ. Negative retention means falling below the rebound start. Ratios are undefined if phase 1 did not decline or the rebound was nonpositive, respectively.
research.conclusion: For lower volatility, MSFT deserves further comparison, with the caveat that its rebound advantage is date-sensitive. For consistency across both window definitions, CRM, PLTR, and OKTA are stronger historical candidates but require a higher risk budget. TEM's recovery efficiency does not erase volatility about 2.5 times NVDA's. The sample helps narrow candidates by objective; it cannot establish an optimal reallocation percentage or promise future returns.
